meta.title: Design review: habit tracker onboarding and home (Android)
meta.scope: Three-step onboarding and the home screen of a habit-tracking app, from three screenshots and a journey description.

goals: Users create their first habit during onboarding

steps.action: Choose a habit and set a time

coverage.limitation: Only one top-level screen was supplied, so navigation structure cannot be judged.
No tokens or library were supplied, and three screens are too few to judge system consistency.

executive_summary.verdict: This is a well-judged first-run flow: it asks for one decision per screen, gets the user to a first habit in two steps, and rewards completion visibly. One real issue was found: the time picker offers no skip, which may block users who do not want reminders. No other evidence-backed problems were found, and none were invented.
strengths: Each onboarding screen has one task and one primary button, so the path to the first habit is two taps long.
The home screen puts today's habit and the streak counter at the top in large type, which matches the return-tomorrow goal.
Copy is short and plain, for example 'What do you want to do daily?'.

findings.title: Reminder time is required to finish setting up a habit

evidence.observation: The time picker is pre-set to 08:00 and the only button is Continue; there is no 'No reminder' or 'Skip' option visible.

findings.impact: Users who do not want notifications must pick a time they will not use, which can cause early notification opt-outs or abandonment at the step that creates the first habit.
findings.recommendation: Add a text option 'No reminder' beside Continue, and ask for notification permission only when a time is chosen.
findings.rationale: Reminders are optional for many users; making them optional protects the first-habit goal and delays the permission prompt until the value is clear. Confidence is medium because a skip may exist outside the visible area.

assumptions: The screenshots show the full height of each screen with no hidden scrolling content.
open_questions: Does the picker allow clearing the time, or does the app always require one?
